transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-07-08 | Start: 13:30 PDT | Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sam Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Gomez (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Cascade Head of ML), Jon Ruiz (Platform Eng), Priya Nair (Procurement)

Auto-summary: 4-week pilot, initial benchmark week, credits cap, success criteria on latency P95 and cost per 1k tokens, SOC2 + KMS confirmed, procurement timeline ~3-6 weeks after pilot if successful.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Sam: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we can see names? great, i'll do a 2-min agenda — quickly cover what redwood proposes for the pilot, then lina will go through the benchmark plan and env needs, then q&a and next steps. sound good?
[00:18] Maya: yep that works, thanks Sam. quick context — we're re-evaluating inference for our in-store personalization engine. main things: latency under 120ms p95, cost targets to be less than current infra, and data residency. we have some compliance constraints, so procurement will want to see SOC2 and KMS support.
[00:36] Sam: understood. lina, want to take the benchmark / sizing?
[00:40] Lina: sure, thanks. so for the POC we recommend a 4-week pilot, with a concentrated 1-week benchmark run in week one where we run representative traffic against Redwood Hosted and a dedicated pool if you want to test that. goal is to measure p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and unit cost after batching.
[01:02] Jon: can you clarify the difference between hosted and dedicated here? we're sensitive to multitenancy and noisy neighbors.
[01:08] Lina: yep, good question. hosted is our managed api with shared infra but isolated at the request layer — it's fast to spin up, lower commitment. dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, consistent throughput, and isolation. latency variability is lower on dedicated, cost higher but more predictable.
[01:25] Maya: for our use case, predictable latency is big — in-store touchscreens can't have spikes. what's the minimum dedicated commit?
[01:33] Sam: typical pilot can use a small dedicated slice — we offer trial credits to offset. for commercial guardrails, we usually propose a credits cap for hosted runs and a separate estimate for a short dedicated eval. we'll include an option: start hosted with credits, if latency variance is too high we spin up a short dedicated run.
[01:50] Priya: on the credits and pilot terms — what are the standard limits? procurement needs to see explicit caps and rollover rules.
[01:58] Sam: standard pilot is 30-60k credit allocation depending on expected tokens; credits cover token usage and basic infra. credits don't roll over; any dedicated reserved capacity is billed by commitment. we can do a limited-term dedicated demo arrangement, but longer dedicated requires contract. we'll send a pilot pricing sheet with exact numbers.
[02:18] Maya: ok. Lina, what info do you need from us to size the benchmark?
[02:22] Lina: we need sample prompts and payload sizes, expected QPS and peak concurrency, and a representative dataset slice. ideally a CSV of 5000 examples and a traffic trace for an hour at peak. even a synthetic distribution is fine. from that we can calculate tokens per request and simulate batching.
[02:40] Jon: on traffic, we expect ~12 qps average, spikes to 80qps for short windows. payloads are usually 150-300 tokens. is that workable?
[02:48] Lina: yes that is workable — we'll design a benchmark with steady-state and spike windows. expected seq len 300 tokens will influence KV cache sizes and memory. we'll note quantization options if you care about cost vs quality tradeoffs.
[03:05] Maya: quality regressions are a concern. we want to preserve metrics for NDCG on rerank and A/B compare. can you do diff checks?
[03:13] Lina: yes, we'll run quality baselines — we ask you to provide scoring function or sample evals. we'll run side-by-side model variants and report token-level cost plus quality.
[03:22] Sam: procurement question — time to contract after pilot?
[03:25] Priya: generally 3-6 weeks, but depends on terms, invertibility, and SSO/KMS compatibility. we need SOC2 report and encryption at rest w/ KMS.
[03:36] Sam: Redwood's private and dedicated options support customer-managed KMS integrations and SOC2 reports available. we'll attach security deck.
[03:42] Maya: great. on benchmarks, will you provide the test harness?
[03:45] Lina: yes, we'll provide a reproducible harness — a small loadgen, config, and prompts, plus a checklist for env variables and network egress. if you want to run in your VPC we can provide a private control plane option but that adds ops time.
[04:00] Jon: network egress — does the hosted option send logs outside our region? we need data residency.
[04:05] Sam: hosted supports region pinning for data residency in most clouds; logs retention policies can be configured. for strict residency you can use private deployment. we'll detail both paths in the docs.
[04:18] Maya: success criteria: propose we set thresholds — p95 < 120ms for inference, avg cost < $0.10 per 1k generated tokens after batching, and quality delta < 2% vs baseline on rerank. are those sensible?
[04:35] Lina: yes sensible. we'll also measure cold-starts and KV hit rates. we'll include automated evals and regression alerts in the report.
[04:44] Priya: the commercial guardrails — we need explicit pilot period, credit cap, what happens at overage, and a path to procurement.
[04:51] Sam: pilot period 4 weeks, credit cap we'll propose as 50k credits to start (we'll tailor once we see sample volumes). overage policy is that we'll notify at 80% and pause further usage if you want; overages billed at list rate unless you sign an MSA. Path to procurement: successful pilot -> term sheet -> PO or MSA signature (typical 3-6 weeks).
[05:12] Maya: can you do a short dedicated run for 48 hours to test variance?
[05:16] Lina: yes we can schedule a dedicated 48-hour window — it requires reserved nodes but we can provision a short-term capacity for benchmarking; cost for that will be outlined.
[05:26] Jon: for the bench we prefer to run both hosted and dedicated for apples-to-apples.
[05:30] Lina: agreed — we will generate two runs with same traffic pattern and compare p95/p50, throughput, and cost per token.
[05:37] Maya: on instrumentation, will you provide per-request latency breakdown?
[05:40] Lina: yes, we'll give token-level latency, batching logs, and KV cache stats.
[05:44] Priya: procurement will ask for SSO/SAML and RBAC controls — are those in place?
[05:49] Sam: yes SSO, SAML, and role-based access are supported; for private we can integrate with your IdP. we'll include security appendix.
[05:58] Maya: sequence of events — outline again so i can show execs.
[06:02] Sam: sure: 1) you share sample data and traffic profile (due 7/14) 2) lina runs a 1-week benchmark (week of 7/14) — includes hosted and a 48hr dedicated window; 3) we deliver report with latency, cost, quality, and recommended config (by 7/25); 4) review with your team and procurement; 5) if ok, we prepare term sheet and start contracting.
[06:24] Maya: sounds good. any blockers on your side for 7/14?
[06:27] Lina: none, assuming we get the samples and access to any sandbox endpoints. we can also run synthetic if needed.
[06:34] Jon: about observability: retention of logs for audits — can you keep logs for 90 days?
[06:39] Sam: yes 90 days is a standard add-on; extended retention is billable. we'll note it in the guardrails.
[06:46] Priya: on pricing, will the pilot credits cover the dedicated 48hr?
[06:50] Sam: we usually separate dedicated demo usage; we can include a modest amount of dedicated time in the credits, but full dedicated evals often require a small reserved fee. we'll put options in the pricing sheet.
[07:03] Maya: any concerns about model drift or reproducibility during the pilot?
[07:07] Lina: we'll pin model versions for the pilot and snapshot configs; if you use in-production model rollouts we'll recommend canary and A/B.
[07:15] Jon: technical question — does redwood support quantized models for CPU inference? we may want lower-cost edge inference later.
[07:21] Lina: we support quantized variants and GPU quantized execution; CPU inference is limited and often slower — we can discuss hybrid routing later. for this pilot we'll focus on GPU inference.
[07:33] Maya: ok great. any other questions?
[07:36] Priya: procurement will want the MSA template. can you send that?
[07:39] Sam: yes we'll attach a redwood MSA template and pilot terms.
[07:44] Maya: timeline looks doable. we'll aim to send sample data by 7/14.
[07:48] Sam: perfect. Lina i'll sync with you on the harness and runbook after.
[07:51] Lina: will do.
[07:54] Sam: recap — deliverables: pricing sheet + pilot credit terms, benchmark harness, security deck, MSA template. next sync after you review the benchmark report, tentatively week of 7/28.
[08:09] Maya: thanks all.
[08:12] Jon: thanks.
[08:13] Priya: thanks.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-IDs and filler, e.g., 'Redwood Dedicate' or 'K V cache' in raw notes.

End of call.
